The learning logic

The next question
has a reason.

The main route combines earlier gaps, a current table focus, written methods, wider topics and due recall. Pupils can begin without choosing a sequence of exercises.

01

Find a starting point

A short warm-up samples the year’s skills. Earlier gaps can lead to supporting questions.

02

Train what matters

Practise a focus table, written methods, weaker skills and a wider curriculum mix.

03

Remember it later

Mistakes get a replay. Earlier facts return on later days, as recall evidence develops.

Prerequisites before repeated frustration

After repeated difficulty, Coach can choose a supporting skill. Recent accurate samples allow progression without treating that early readiness as lasting mastery.

Mistakes after a gap

A missed question can return after other questions. Repeating an answer immediately after seeing it is different from retrieving it later.

Separate fact-family evidence

Multiplication, inverse division for a divisor, and missing factors are recorded separately. Related facts are connected without letting one answer prove every representation.

Reviews on later days

Successful independent recall can advance scheduled reviews through 1, 3, 7, 14, 30 and 60 days. Mathematical help or an error resets the recall interval.

Promotion needs more than points

The current year’s practice and practical goals must be complete before a mixed promotion match can award the next academy year. XP, credits and club choices are separate cosmetic progression.

Keep returning after success

Earlier facts remain in review after promotion. No app can guarantee permanent memory, and practical teaching and explanation remain valuable.
